reason: None of the cited evidence addresses the SFE, dislocation dynamics, or mechanical properties of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi. E1 discusses AuCu nanowires, E2 concerns SRO effects in refractory HEAs, E3 is a general introduction to HEAs, and E4 describes deformation mechanisms in Al0.3CoCrFeNi, none of which support the specific premises about CoCrFeNiTi.
premises: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in solid-solution state has intrinsically high stacking fault energy (SFE)
High SFE enables easy activation of multiple slip systems and rapid dislocation cross-slip
Rapid cross-slip inhibits dislocation pile-up and work hardening
Inhibited work hardening limits hardness and strength while promoting plasticity and machinability
